blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An ML model reports an RUL of 1 year for a 70-year-old switch. Its training clipped every target to between 1 and 40 years. The switch type's fitted curve gives this switch a median remaining life of 9 years. How should a planner read the 1?

options.text: As a 50% chance that the switch fails within the year, since an RUL is its median remaining life
options.says: An RUL may be a mean, a median, a quantile or a time to a threshold; taken as a median, a floored 1 claims a 50% PoF that the curve does not support.

options.text: As the lowest value the model can output, which cannot rank this switch against other old ones
options.says: Right: at the floor the prediction carries no information; GridCap's ten assets at RUL 1 have medians from 3.2 to 21.5 years.

options.text: As a failure within the year, since a useful life of one year ends when the switch breaks down
options.says: Useful life often ends at a threshold, such as a health index limit, not at a failure.

options.text: As the mean remaining life, since a regression model predicts the mean of its target in every case
options.says: A model trained on a quantile loss predicts that quantile, and a clipped target is neither; ask which statistic it is.

origin.section: Ask What the Number Is: Which Statistic, Which End Point, What Error

questions.stem: Two motors are both 25 years old, and the analytics team gives each a median remaining life of 12 years. Motor M's type has shape 1.1 and motor N's type has shape 5. Which motor is more likely to fail in the coming year?

options.text: Both alike, since equal ages and equal median remaining lives fix the chance for next year
options.says: Many curves pass through one median; the lesson's two assets with one age and one median differ by a factor of two.

options.text: Motor N, since a larger shape gives a higher failure rate in the next year at any age
options.says: With the median fixed, a large shape bunches failures near the median, so next year is safer; the lesson's shape-6 asset had the lower PoF.

options.text: Neither can be judged, since a median remaining life says nothing about the next year
options.says: With the shape known, the median fixes the scale, and the curve gives next year's PoF.

options.text: Motor M, since a shape near 1 spreads the failures out instead of bunching them later
options.says: Right: on these numbers M's next-year PoF is about 5.5% and N's about 2.4%.

origin.section: RUL Alone Does Not Fix the PoF: the Shape Decides

questions.stem: A breaker is 20 years old, its type's Weibull shape is 2, and the model reports its median RUL as 10 years. Which scale makes 10 years the median remaining life of this breaker?

options.text: About 26.9 years, from ((30^2 - 20^2) / ln 2)^(1/2), counted given it works at 20
options.says: Right: R(a + m)/R(a) = 1/2 gives eta = (((a + m)^beta - a^beta) / ln 2)^(1/beta).

options.text: About 36.0 years, from (30^2 / ln 2)^(1/2), the age at which half of new units fail
options.says: That makes 30 the median lifetime of a new breaker; it ignores that this one has already lasted 20 years.

options.text: About 12.0 years, from 10 / (ln 2)^(1/2), the curve of a new unit with that median
options.says: That treats the breaker as new, with a median lifetime of 10; the condition must start from its age of 20.

options.text: About 30.0 years, from 20 + 10, since the scale is the expected age at failure
options.says: The scale is the age by which 63% of a fleet has failed, not the expected or median age at failure.

origin.section: To Use an RUL, Make It a Point on a Curve
